flags.observation: One setup-punch, but no beat says who speaks or what the satirical premise is; insider references stop at the card names Rhodes and Milner.
Opener "At the dinner table." restates beat 2's "At family dinner" without advancing; no therefore/but link into the first card.
Line ends in the fragment "sovereign natural resources"; the card's claim about uppity states vanishes, leaving an unexplained noun pile.
Cut to "owns companies" drops the card's turn "that dictate it"; the line loses its punch.
Stacked colon chain "Milner's round table: The Five Star Slush Fund:" sounds like a renamed card; 112 characters, hard in one breath.
Callback opener is a bare name label with no causal or twist link from BlackRock's Aladdin AI to the slush fund.
Ending "surface world to destroy itself." drops the card's waiting verb; the fragment reads garbled.
"white peacekeepers" turns the card's uniform colour ("The peacekeepers wear white") into a phrase heard as race; singles out a group.
"disguised elite debauchery" flips the card: the operation was disguised as debauchery, not the debauchery disguised.
"Cecil's original deal:" calls back card 1 but gives no logical link to deepfake extortion; the double colon stalls the breath.
"Flexner medicine, petroleum-based patentable extraction" is a noun stack; the Flexner Report claim no longer reads as a sentence.
Openers "Cold war.", "Patent.", "Chemical.", "Lab bench." are one-word topic labels at fixed three-beat spacing: props, not people, no therefore/but.
Victim line compressed to "dead babies for tests"; the card's stealing and radiation context dropped, leaving bare shock wording.
Name cut to "The Scamdemic"; dropping "Board Game" removes the parody marker, so a health-conspiracy label is voiced straight.
Card's ironic turn "It's not a conspiracy; it's just excellent planning!" shrinks to "planning." and the joke no longer lands.
Line recites the power rule "automatically reclassify them as anxiety-related"; the lore's claim about patenting oncology treatments is gone.
Outro "isn't selling research. He's selling a subscription" is a generic isn't-X-it's-Y aphorism; fits any conspiracy song, names no deck image.
Outro calls back neither the intro's dinner-table uncle nor the PowerPoint, and does not echo the deck title.
